summary: A short correction to RFC 70: a statement in the FORTRAN program on page 7 should read N=1.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 228 corrects one line in a FORTRAN program printed in RFC 70. The line should read N=1.

questions: what should the corrected fortran line say
subtitle: A one-line correction to a FORTRAN program in RFC 70.

tldr.problem: A statement in the FORTRAN program on page 7 of RFC 70 needed correction.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 228 says that the second statement before statement 20 should read N=1.
tldr.outcome: The document updates RFC 70 and contains no other technical correction.

today: RFC 228 updates RFC 70. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 228.

sections.title: The Program Line
sections.content: RFC 228 is titled “Clarification” and updates RFC 70. It identifies a specific line in the FORTRAN program on page 7 of that earlier RFC: the second statement before statement 20.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC points to one statement in the program printed in RFC 70. It identifies the statement by its position on the page.

sections.title: The Corrected Text
sections.content: The second statement before statement 20 in the FORTRAN program on page 7 of RFC 70 should read N=1. This is the correction supplied by RFC 228.
sections.plainLanguage: The corrected line is N=1. No other change is specified.

sections.title: Scope of the Clarification
sections.content: The memo contains a single correction to the earlier program. Its header says that it updates RFC 70 and lists no obsolete document. The remaining text includes a note about preparing the RFC in machine-readable form for the online archive.
sections.plainLanguage: The clarification is limited to one program statement. The RFC also includes an archival note.
